A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 22-page versions of AvAtar: Learning to Align via Active Optimal Transport. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main paper and Appendices A–D without unresolved material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on network alignment, image-text retrieval, and image-text grounding in Section 5, plus additional evaluations and synthetic-graph scalability results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark Tables 3–5, ablation Tables 6–7, and the additional experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The utility functions, gradient-based query impact, adjoint linear system, conjugate-gradient computation, and query procedure in Algorithm 1 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four network datasets, CIFAR-10-C and ImageNet-C retrieval tasks, COCO and Flickr30K Entities grounding tasks, and synthetic Erdős–Rényi graph scalability scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables and appendix analyses, including GibbsMatchings and TopMatchings for network alignment and FINAL + Attent in Table 8.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 retains the same 20% initial supervision, 20% query budget over ten rounds, evaluation metrics, and default baseline hyperparameters. The remaining experimental protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical convergence, hyperparameter sensitivity, sparse-versus-dense computation, posterior-versus-uniform aggregation, transport-plan visualization, and scalability analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 states in both versions that results are averaged over five runs with randomly selected initial supervision. No repeated-run information or uncertainty reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings in Tables 3–9 and Figures 1–11 are unchanged, including the appendix comparisons, runtime results, and hyperparameter studies.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, gradient derivation, convergence and complexity statements, and proofs in Appendix A are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about active OT alignment, gradient-based candidate selection, theoretical guarantees, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations remain identical. Appendix D retains the same qualifications concerning potentially reduced benefits for geometric matching and the unresolved extension to neural OT.

D1.justification: Implementation and experimental details in Appendix B, hardware specifications, and the code/data access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion in Section 6, and positioning relative to previous alignment methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The acknowledgment on page 10 adds NSF grant 2433309. The first-page arXiv version/date stamp also updates; research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added grant number slightly changes acknowledgment line wrapping on page 10, and the first-page version stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and other page layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds NSF grant 2433309 to the funding acknowledgment and updates the version stamp, with only local text reflow. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information—including the appendices—are unchanged, so this administrative revision does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
